questions.stem: In economics, demand for a commodity means the quantity that consumers are

options.text: willing and able to buy at a given price in a given period
in need of, whether or not they can pay for it
offered for sale by producers at a given price
able to buy only when prices are falling

questions.explanation: Demand requires both willingness and ability to pay, and it must be tied to a stated price and period. A desire without purchasing power is a mere want, not demand.

distractorRationale.b: Need without ability to pay is desire; it does not register in any market
distractorRationale.c: Quantity offered for sale is supply, not demand
distractorRationale.d: Demand exists at every price, high or low; only its size changes

questions.stem: A normal demand curve slopes downwards from left to right because

options.text: producers supply more as price rises
consumers buy more of a commodity as its price falls
the cost of production falls as output rises
government fixes prices below the market level

questions.explanation: The negative slope simply pictures the law of demand: a lower price raises real purchasing power and makes the good cheaper than its substitutes, so more is bought.

distractorRationale.a: That describes the upward-sloping supply curve
distractorRationale.c: Falling unit costs concern production, and would affect supply rather than demand
distractorRationale.d: Price control shifts attention to shortages; it does not explain the shape of the curve

questions.stem: From the demand schedule for tomatoes — ₦500: 10 baskets, ₦400: 20 baskets, ₦300: 35 baskets, ₦200: 55 baskets, ₦100: 80 baskets — by how many baskets does quantity demanded rise when the price falls from ₦400 to ₦200? Give a number only.
questions.explanation: At ₦400 buyers take 20 baskets and at ₦200 they take 55 baskets, so the rise is 55 − 20 = 35 baskets. Because the good's own price caused the change, this is an extension of demand along the same curve.

questions.stem: An increase in the minimum wage causes households to buy more beef. In terms of the demand curve for beef, this is shown by

options.text: a movement down along the existing demand curve
a shift of the whole demand curve to the right
a shift of the whole demand curve to the left
a movement up along the existing demand curve

questions.explanation: The price of beef has not changed; income has. Any non-price factor shifts the entire curve, and since beef is a normal good, higher income increases demand at every price, moving the curve rightward.

distractorRationale.a: Movements along the curve occur only when the good's own price changes
distractorRationale.c: A leftward shift would mean demand fell, which is what a fall in income would cause
distractorRationale.d: An upward movement along the curve would follow a rise in the price of beef itself

questions.stem: Cars and petrol are said to be in

options.text: competitive demand
composite demand
complementary demand
derived demand

questions.explanation: The two goods are used together and one is of little use without the other, so a rise in the price of petrol reduces the demand for cars. Goods related in this way are complements, also described as being in joint demand.

distractorRationale.a: Competitive demand applies to substitutes such as rice and spaghetti
distractorRationale.b: Composite demand applies to one good wanted for several different uses, such as maize
distractorRationale.d: Derived demand applies to a good wanted for what it helps produce, such as cement for houses

questions.stem: The demand for labour by a bakery is an example of

options.text: direct demand
derived demand
competitive demand
composite demand

questions.explanation: The bakery does not want bakers for their own sake; it wants them because bread is wanted. Demand for a factor of production is therefore derived from the demand for the product it makes.

distractorRationale.a: Direct demand is for goods that satisfy a want immediately, such as a loaf of bread itself
distractorRationale.c: Competitive demand concerns substitutes competing for the same buyer
distractorRationale.d: Composite demand concerns one commodity wanted for several different purposes

questions.stem: Which of the following best illustrates an exception to the law of demand?

options.text: A fall in the price of rice leads households to buy more rice
Sales of a luxury wristwatch rise after its price is doubled, because owning it now signals wealth
A rise in the price of beef causes buyers to switch to chicken
Demand for umbrellas rises during the rainy season

questions.explanation: Goods of ostentation, or Veblen goods, are bought partly because they are expensive, so quantity demanded can rise with price. That is a genuine reversal of the law of demand.

distractorRationale.a: This is the law of demand behaving exactly as predicted
distractorRationale.c: This is the substitution effect, which supports rather than contradicts the law
distractorRationale.d: A seasonal rise is a shift of the whole demand curve caused by a non-price factor, not an exception to the law

questions.stem: A fall in the price of a commodity causes an increase in demand for that commodity.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: False. A fall in the good's own price causes an extension of demand — a movement down along the same demand curve. An increase in demand means the whole curve shifts rightward, and only non-price factors such as income or taste can do that.

distractorRationale.a: This confuses movement along a curve with a shift of the curve, the most heavily penalised error in this topic
